identity: Short, unedited Modern Standard Arabic opinion composition about social media (وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي) and its effects. Paragraph 1 asserts its impact on society and the individual and issues a prescriptive warning to users; paragraph 2 lists benefits to individuals (influencer-driven commerce, fame, money earned by posting for merchants and companies). The register is amateur student-essay / user-generated web prose, not edited nonfiction. Diagnostics: a malformed word at 94 (تشاجرة, evidently for تجارة); a non-standard collocation at 19-20 (يجب لمن rather than يجب على من); an أما-topic at 33 with no answering ف; heavy lexical repetition (وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي four times, الشهرة twice inside one clause); and argument carried by long chains of coordinated masdar NPs instead of finite clauses. Nearest doctrine bin is section B / section L (modern expository), but with far fewer finite verbs and a much higher noun-coordination ratio than edited expository prose. 105 tokens, two paragraphs, <NL> at index 32.
law: Expository rhythm at the long end of the LAW 6 section-B/L band, roughly 12-18 tokens per unit: this author packs a whole argument into one coordinated masdar chain, so clause count is low while token count per unit is high. Only three kinds of site take a boundary. (1) A discourse connective that opens a conclusion or a new point attaches FORWARD, closing the unit before it: لذلك at 18, أيضا at 63, وأيضا at 89. (2) The appositive-elaboration frame [و]منها plus a new subject NP is a full nominal clause with its own new argument, so LAW 1 / C4 cuts before it; the frame repeats three times, which makes it LAW 3 parallelism as well: ومنها التجارة at 45, منها تصميم at 80, منها شركات المقاولات at 99. (3) The two free boundaries: the token before <NL> (31) and the final token (104). Everything else that looks like a joint is phrase-level و coordinating nouns or masdars, and the LAW 1 exception forbids cutting those (المجتمع والفرد; انتشارها وحب ... وإدمان ... وتقليدهم; الانتباه وعدم نشر; التجارة ... ودعايتهم ... ونشرها ... والاستفادة; تصميم ونشر; الشهرة والمال). Trailing adjuncts stay with their main clause per LAW 4: the بسبب-PP at 9, the التي-relative at 28, the للحصول purpose PP at 74, the بمختلف الطرق PP at 78.
reasoning: Calibration first (LAW 6, step zero). Reading the opening 40 tokens: no narrative verbs, no dialogue, no isnad, no page furniture; a thesis clause, a causal PP with a four-item NP list, a prescriptive لذلك move, then an أما-fronted topic. That is expository, so the target is the 12-20 band, not the 7-token graded-reader band. LAW 0 still governs the coin flips (I under-cut 4.8 to 1, so ties go to CUT), but LAW 0 also says reconstruct the ink, and this author's ink is thin: he writes long run-ons and uses و as his only glue. Eight boundaries over 105 tokens gives 13.1 tokens per unit, which is what both paragraphs actually support. || SITE @17 للبعض / @18 لذلك - CUT, hi. لذلك is a consequence connective opening the prescriptive move of the essay. The unit before it is complete (thesis plus بسبب-PP whose object is a closed list), and لذلك brings a new predicate and new arguments. Whether the source had a full stop or a comma before it, the LAW 0 corollary turns both into a boundary. || SITE @8 والفرد / @9 بسبب - NO CUT. بسبب is a preposition trailing its main clause. LAW 4 forbids cutting before a trailing adjunct, even though an untrained writer might plausibly have fragmented here. || SITES @11 وحب, @14 وإدمان, @16 وتقليدهم - NO CUTS. Four bare NPs governed by one بسبب. The LAW 1 exception is explicit that و joining nouns never cuts, and the gold precedent أفرادا ودولا ومؤسسات دولية was kept whole inside its segment. I note the LAW 0 pull toward cutting a comma-set list and resist it: section B5 puts the boundaries at the commas that BRACKET a parenthetical, never between the و-joined items themselves. || SITE @23 وعدم - NO CUT. الانتباه وعدم نشر are two masdars under one يجب: no new predicate, no new argument. Splitting a topic NP from its predicate is a section-K3 caption rule, not an expository rule. || SITE @44 المجالات / @45 ومنها - CUT, med. ومنها التجارة is a nominal clause: fronted predicate PP plus a new subject NP. The LAW 1 test (does a new argument follow the و) answers yes. This is exactly the وتشمل / وهي / والفائدة appositive-continuation shape that my section-L note records as the one residual leak where the gold cuts and I keep absorbing. Cutting. || SITES @53 ودعايتهم, @55 ونشرها, @60 والاستفادة - NO CUTS, and this is a deliberate decision against the LAW 0 density pressure. Keeping them welded leaves 45-62 at 18 tokens, the longest unit in the document, which is uncomfortable; but splitting a masdar list is precisely the false cut that the LAW 1 exception exists to prevent, and my batch-1 false cuts clustered in exactly this shape. || SITE @62 منها / @63 أيضا - CUT AT 62, lo. This is the hardest site in the document. A boundary here is near-certain; only its POSITION is at issue, so LAW 0 gives no help and the exposure is a pure LAW 5 off-by-one. Backward reading: والاستفادة منها أيضا closes the masdar list as (and benefiting from them as well), which suits an author this redundant (he writes بالاستفادة من الشهرة and then للحصول على الشهرة nine tokens later). Forward reading: أيضا opens the second major point of the paragraph (fame and money, as against commerce before it), the calqued (Also, ...) sentence opener that is endemic in this register. I take forward, on the LAW 4 mirror rule that short adverbials attach to what follows - the rule I earned by placing a boundary one unit late at doc_3f6c5f1e305a @1922, where I attached على ما يبدو backward and the gold opened the next sentence with it. Corroboration from inside this document: the same author uses وأيضا at 89 as a forward-facing transition, so أيضا is his connective, not his tail. Boundary at 62. || SITES @74 للحصول, @78 بمختلف - NO CUTS. Trailing purpose and manner PPs (LAW 4). The unit 63-79 is 17 tokens with a single finite verb (بدأ) and no second predicate anywhere, so there is nothing to cut. || SITE @79 الطرق / @80 منها - CUT, med. Asyndetic منها plus new subject NP: the same frame as 45 with the و dropped. The LAW 3 discriminator applies - this is repetition of a frame, not mere sequence, so it cuts (the section-F يكبر / يزداد طولا / يتضخم precedent), and it is not the plain asyndetic narrative continuation that produced my batch-1 false cuts at doc_226fc860e550 @710 and doc_56781db1019f @242. For cutting: و plus an additive adverb is a discourse-marker cluster rather than simple phrasal coordination, the author has already used أيضا as an opener at 63, and LAW 0 puts genuine coin flips on the cut side at about five to one. Coordination inside a single NP. || SITE @98 الشركات / @99 منها - CUT, med. Third instance of the منها frame, same argument as 80, and the third instance is what confirms the parallelism reading for all three.
